title: Return to the Wurstreich - A Look at Grime & Gold at the Ghostgates and Die Wurst issue 2
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pms2oKZcuqo

New material has arrived for **Dungeon Degenerates: Hand of Doom**, and Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to the Wurstreich to look at two pieces of it — with genuine enthusiasm and a real reservation.

First is Die Wurst issue 2, the official zine, which carries almost no gameplay material and is all the better for it: articles on Ralph Bakshi's animation, on Uriah Heep (he singles out Demons and Wizards), on the 1970s model kits that clearly fed Sean Äaberg's art, and a continuation of the Satanic Panic piece. The gaming centrepiece is Eric Bouchard's guide to running Dungeon Degenerates as an RPG — an idea Daniel had already floated himself, and one the game's stat and dice systems support almost without modification. An editor's note confirms an official RPG is intended, back-burnered while Sean recovers from a stroke.

The main draw is Grime & Gold at the Ghostgates: a full choose-your-own-adventure dungeon module tied to a specific board location, playable as an interlude mid-campaign. Daniel is thrilled by the format and immediately imagines one for every landmark on the map. But quality control bites — a page of rules is missing outright, the wandering-monster rules still absent even after Sean posted errata. His advice is to wait for the corrected printing.

----

Daniel wants a choose-your-own-adventure module for every landmark on a board he already owns. Which game's map would you most like expanded that way?
